title: Flatbrød (Norwegian crisp flatbread)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for rolling

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan). Mix both flours with the salt, sugar and baking powder in a large bowl.
Pour in the melted butter and the buttermilk and stir to a stiff dough, adding a splash more liquid only if it will not come together. Let it rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces. On a floured surface, roll each piece out as thin as you can, as thin as paper if possible, keeping a round or oval shape.
Prick the sheets all over with a fork or a knobbly rolling pin so that they do not puff up.
Lay each sheet on a baking tray lined with paper and bake for 5 to 8 minutes until crisp and lightly browned at the edges. Watch closely, because they burn quickly at this thinness.
Cool completely on a rack. Break into pieces and serve with soup, cheese or smoked fish; stored dry in a tin, they keep for weeks.

title: Julekake (Norwegian Christmas bread with cardamom and fruit)

ingredients.name: egg, plus 1 beaten egg for glazing
candied peel or mixed candied fruit

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt in a large bowl. Add the lukewarm milk, melted butter and one egg and knead for about 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough in a warm place for about an hour, until doubled in size.
Knead the raisins, candied peel and almonds into the dough, then shape it into a round loaf and set it on a lined baking tray or in a round tin.
Cover and let it rise for another 30 to 40 minutes until puffy. Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan).
Brush the loaf with beaten egg and bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool on a rack. Serve in slices, plain or toasted, with butter and brown or white cheese.

title: Multekrem (Norwegian cloudberry cream)

ingredients.name: cloudberries, fresh or thawed from frozen (or cloudberry jam as a substitute)
krumkake or small biscuits to serve

steps: Set aside a few of the nicest berries for decoration. If your berries are very firm, warm the rest briefly in a small pan with a spoonful of the sugar until they just soften, then let them cool completely.
Pour the cream into a cold bowl and whip it with the remaining sugar and the vanilla sugar until it holds soft peaks. Avoid going further, as the berries will thicken it slightly.
Fold the cooled berries into the cream with a few gentle strokes so the colour stays marbled and the berries stay mostly whole.
Spoon the cream into glasses and chill for at least an hour. Top with the reserved berries and serve with a crisp krumkake or other thin biscuit.

title: Smultringer (Norwegian cardamom doughnuts)
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar for a couple of minutes until pale, then stir in the cream, melted butter and lemon zest.
Mix the flour, baking powder, cardamom and salt, and fold them into the egg mixture to make a soft but workable dough. Chill it for at least 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1 cm thick and cut rings with a doughnut cutter, or cut a larger round and punch out the middle.
Heat the oil to about 175 C. Fry a few doughnuts at a time for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through.
Lift them out onto kitchen paper to drain, then roll in sugar while still warm. Serve fresh, with coffee.

title: Sodd (Trøndelag mutton and meatball soup)

ingredients.name: mutton or lamb shoulder, on the bone
salt, plus more for the meatballs
chopped parsley or chives to serve

steps: Put the meat on the bone into a large pot, cover with the cold water, add a tablespoon of salt and bring slowly to a simmer. Skim off the grey foam that rises.
Keep the broth at a very gentle simmer for about two hours, until the meat is tender and pulls easily from the bone.
Meanwhile, work the minced meat with a teaspoon of salt, the ginger, nutmeg, milk and starch until the mixture is smooth and sticky, then shape it into small walnut-sized balls.
Lift the cooked meat out of the pot, strain the broth, and return it to a clean pot. Slip the meatballs into the barely simmering broth and poach them for about 10 minutes until firm.
In a separate pan of salted water, boil the potatoes and carrots until just tender. Traditionally they are cooked apart so that the broth stays clear.
Cut the meat from the bones into bite-sized pieces. Put meat, meatballs, potatoes and carrots into deep bowls and ladle the hot broth over, finishing with a little parsley or chives.
